p.x:
My candid take on the DMT laser claims:

For context, Danny Goler discovered that if you look at a flat laser projected on a wall (so it appears as a line) while on a small to medium dose of DMT, you can see a strange, alphabet-like "code" within it. This visual effect resembles an alien language. It's evocative of the Matrix simulation aesthetics ("reality code").

Concretely, what this code looks like is the patterns you see in the picture: Danny confirmed this.

In essence, we’re dealing with cymatics.

The "code" appears as you’d expect if no information were actually being transmitted. These patterns are non-linear, high-frequency resonant modes of the visual field. For context, see Stephen Lehar’s work on the grassfire algorithm and shock scaffold theory of visual processing (from "The Constructive Aspect of Visual Processing"). QRI has been aware of this phenomenon for quite some time. This isn’t evidence of intelligent design, communication, or purpose. It's pure physics: the natural behavior of non-linear wave dynamics.

From a research perspective, the laser phenomenology setup is interesting because it selectively amplifies high-frequency cymatic patterns. It could serve as a userul addition to a suite of psychophysics tools for psychedelic research.

That said:

1. Danny claims there are other phenomena visible in this setup that he hasn’t disclosed yet. He’s keeping these findings private for now, aiming to preserve the integrity of future independent reports.

2. DMT remains an incredibly weird and powerful state of consciousness, full stop. However, my focus here is on its phenomenal character, the mathematics, the physics, and the algorithmic frameworks for understanding this psychedelic state (e.g., hyperbolic geometry of DMT experiences, neural annealing, topological segmentation, structural theories of valence, and high-quality replication engines).

If I were trying to demonstrate the existence of genuine "higher intelligences" accessible through DMT, my emphasis would be on the novel computational properties of the state, especially at high doses. Notably:

A) entities capable of coloring surfaces rapidly (cf. the four-color theorem)

B) Indra’s Net phenomenology 

C) skillful projection and dimensionality reduction operations seemingly controlled by other beings

D) implicit higher-dimensional rotations, and,

E) topological extrema finding

To me, these are the kinds of truly bizarre and innovative aspects of the DMT state. By comparison, cymatics are well-known and relatively unremarkable.

Note: I mostly agree with Alien Insects’ (@alieninsect) take on this topic. I respect Danny's curiosity and earnestness and really enjoy his company when I've had the chance to meet him. The perspective above is simply the key QRI-specific view I think has been missing in the discourse. If you’re interested, there will be a live debate between them on December 10th where you can go deep into the discussion. Also @cube_flipper agrees with the assessment presented in this post, for what is worth (IMO a lot! Great phenomenologist).
